description: Our mission is to construct a earth jukebox natural disaster predictor
summary: Team Kungfu Warriors developed the Earth Jukebox for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. This accessible observatory transforms open NASA datasets into a 20-day predictive risk tool for wildfires, floods, and tsunamis. It delivers instant localized emergency contacts, actionable safety guides, and multimodal audio-visual features with strict privacy protections.
details: The Earth Jukebox is an accessible web-based observatory developed by Team Kungfu Warriors for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, designed to turn complex open NASA data into actionable, easy-to-understand environmental risk insights. By clicking anywhere on a map or tapping user location, individuals receive a 20-day outlook for wildfires, floods, and tsunamis, acomplete with daily scores, uncertainty bands, and peak hazard days derived from sources like NASA POWER, NASA FIRMS, NASA EONET, USGS, and Open-Meteo. The project solves the fragmentation of safety information by providing three critical answers in one place: risk exposure, curated emergency numbers and official agencies for over 45 countries, and step-by-step guidance on what to do. Built with a strict "Trust by Design" architecture, the application ensures that AI is fenced in to reword server-computed facts without generating phone links, guarantees that missing data sources show as unavailable rather than false zeros, and operates completely privately without accounts, cookies, or tracking. Furthermore, it features robust accessibility standards including screen reader support, keyboard navigation, text alternatives for charts, and a Web Audio engine alongside spoken briefings that make environmental data something users can see, hear, and act on.
